correctness.rationale: For six arbitrary continuous unimodular phases, common-phase and linear-phase invariance normalize endpoints, giving two interior mirror-pair parametrizations. The exact expansion E=5+4F and four corner coefficients p_i is checked independently. Exact symbolic expansion of the package's four bivariate identities 2D p_i=||z_i||^2 and z1·z4−z2·z3=−4DB returned zero as polynomial identities; 200 random phase samples also agreed with E=5+4F (consistency only). Cauchy–Schwarz yields sqrt(p1p4)+sqrt(p2p3)>=2|B|, and a valid AM-GM decomposition proves F>=0 for all real phases, including tangent-half-angle poles by continuity. Independent exact sixth-root ring calculation gives |C_1|²=...=|C_5|²=1, E=5, L4^4=36+2E=46 and MF=18/5. This is a universal proof, not a finite search.
residual_risks: Applies to length exactly six, all complex unimodular coefficients, aperiodic correlations; no complete equality classification.
The checked polynomial SOS identities are exact but do not independently establish historical novelty.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: the 1965 generalized Barker sequence establishes a sextic-root witness/peak sidelobes, not the global sum-of-squared sidelobe optimum for arbitrary continuous phases. The complete Borwein–Ferguson 2005 paper lists E=5.000 for n=6 but expressly describes stochastic local optimization and statistical confidence, not a certificate of a universal minimum. A distinct published length-five result does not imply the length-six lower bound; other six-mode Fourier-support papers concern different support sets. Targeted aliases/radar/merit searches found no full continuous global proof; a search failure alone is not taken as novelty proof.
residual_risks: An earlier full continuum proof may exist under older radar/phase-code terminology not retrieved; targeted searches do not exclude it.
The six-phase Hessian result is only strict local minimality, not a competing global proof.
No equality-orbit classification or higher-length extrapolation.
